sources.entry: mongoDB.app - The easiest way to get started with mongoDB on the Mac.

summary.one_liner: mongoDB.app is a macOS app that bundles MongoDB binaries so you can run a MongoDB server by downloading, dragging to Applications, and double-clicking.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Mac application that packages mongoDB binaries for easy launch: download, drag to the Applications folder, and double-click. Each release's version number indicates the bundled mongoDB version, with a separate build number for the app itself. It explains how to add the bundled mongo binaries to the shell PATH, either through ~/.bash_profile or via path_helper with /etc/paths.d. It also mentions installation through Homebrew Cask using the gcollazo-mongodb cask. The README lists Redis.app and RabbitMQ.app as similar projects.
use_cases: run a local mongodb server on a mac
use mongo shell binaries from the terminal
install mongodb on macos with homebrew cask
start a development database on a laptop
how_to_run: Download the app from the project's releases
Drag MongoDB.app to the Applications folder
brew cask install gcollazo-mongodb (optional, Homebrew Cask)
notable: Drag-and-drop macOS app that bundles mongoDB binaries
Version numbers track the bundled mongoDB version, with a separate build number
Optional PATH setup for the bundled mongo binaries
caveats: Mac-only; the README describes macOS installation and paths only
README gives no details on configuration, data directory, or the bundled mongoDB version beyond the versioning scheme
The README does not state a license
